description: Make compatibility rules bidirectional and support the compatible type (F-2). CompatibilityService only fires when selections[attribute_id] === option_id, only handles type 'incompatible', disables only the target (asymmetric/evadable), and ignores type 'compatible'. Make incompatibility symmetric and implement compatible semantics, preserving human-readable reason strings. Independent of FEAT-003; depends on FEAT-001 (factories, single BOM path).
steps: In CompatibilityService::getDisabledOptions(): for type 'incompatible', keep the existing direction (trigger option selected on attribute_id -> disable target_option_id on target_attribute_id) AND add the reverse direction (target_option_id selected on target_attribute_id -> disable option_id on attribute_id). Use rule->reason ?? 'Incompatible with current selection.' as the reason on both directions. Keep string-safe comparisons via (string) casts.

Implement type 'compatible': when a compatible rule's trigger (option_id on attribute_id) is selected, restrict target_attribute_id to ONLY the listed target_option_id(s) across all matching compatible rules for that (trigger, target_attribute_id) pair — build the allow-list, then disable every OTHER active option of target_attribute_id with a reason like 'Only compatible with current selection.' Load the target attribute's active options to compute the complement.
Preserve Phase 1 behavior: keep consuming product->compatibilityRules() which already filters is_active; do not weaken that filter.

Add tests/Feature/CompatibilityRulesTest.php (Pest): (a) incompatible is symmetric — selecting A disables B, and in a fresh evaluation selecting B disables A (both orders); (b) a compatible rule restricts target_attribute_id to the listed option(s) when the trigger is selected (a non-listed option of the target attribute is disabled); (c) reason strings are present on disabled entries. Run Pint and targeted tests, then the full suite.
acceptance_criteria: Incompatible rules disable in both directions (A->B and B->A) regardless of selection order (CompatibilityRulesTest passes).
A compatible rule, when triggered, allows only its listed target option(s) and disables the rest of that target attribute's active options.
Human-readable reason strings are preserved/returned for every disabled option.
Phase 1 is_active filtering on compatibility rules is preserved.
findings:
DONE. Full suite green: 39 passed (92 assertions); CompatibilityRulesTest adds 3 tests.

=== CompatibilityService::getDisabledOptions (app/Services/Configurator/CompatibilityService.php) ===
Return shape UNCHANGED: array<int attribute_id, array<int option_id, string reason>> i.e. [attribute_id => [option_id => reason]]. ConfiguratorService::evaluate merges this with rule-driven disabled_options via the union operator (numeric keys preserved) and validate() reads $options[$selected] as the reason string -- shape stays compatible.

=== incompatible (now SYMMETRIC) ===
Per rule, two independent directions via helper applyIncompatibleRule(): if trigger (option_id on attribute_id) selected => disable target_option_id on target_attribute_id; if target_option_id on target_attribute_id selected => disable option_id on attribute_id. Both use rule->reason ?? 'Incompatible with current selection.'. Comparisons via (string) casts in isSelected().

=== compatible (restrict-to-listed) ===
applyCompatibleRules() builds an allow-list PER target_attribute_id ACROSS all triggered compatible rules first (so two compatible rules for the same (trigger,target_attr) union their allowed target options instead of cancelling each other), then loads AttributeOption where attribute_id=target and is_active=true and disables every active option NOT in the allow-list with rule->reason ?? 'Only compatible with current selection.'. Uses ??= so an incompatible-set reason on the same (attr,option) is not overwritten.

=== Phase 1 preserved ===
Still consumes product->compatibilityRules() (which filters is_active=true); only is_active target options are considered for the compatible complement. No filter weakened.

=== Test ===
tests/Feature/CompatibilityRulesTest.php resolves the service via app(CompatibilityService::class). Covers symmetric incompatible (both orders), compatible restrict-to-listed (non-listed option disabled, listed one not), and null-reason fallback to the default string.

=== disabled-options shape ===
[attribute_id (int) => [option_id (int) => reason (string)]].
